Why Do You Need an Attorney?

Insurance companies are notorious for taking advantage of injured clients. With an attorney by your side, however, you can fight for maximum financial compensation and protect your rights.
Common Off-Road Recreational Vehicle Accident Injuries

Off-road recreational vehicles often take the form of four-wheelers and three-wheelers: open-top vehicles that hardly protect their passengers in accidents. In an accident such as a collision or rollover, an off-road vehicle rider and any passengers can suffer significant injuries, such as:
Bone fractures
Crush injuries
Muscle, tendon and other soft-tissue injuries
Cuts, scrapes and lacerations
Concussions and traumatic brain injuries
Back and spinal cord injuries
Neck injuries
Contusions
Severed limbs
Catastrophic injuries
Wrongful death

Injuries can be especially severe if the off-road recreational vehicle accident involves a collision with a standard motor vehicle. Even with a helmet and other protective gear, a rider can suffer life-altering injuries in this type of accident.
Primary Causes of Off-Road Recreational Vehicle Accidents

Determining fault for your accident is one of the first steps in obtaining financial compensation in Colorado. Although many different things can cause these collisions, some of the most common causes of ATV and other off-road recreational vehicle accidents in Boulder are:
Inexperienced riders
Unsupervised child operators
Property defects, such as rocks or potholes
Faulty vehicle design or manufacturing defects
An off-road vehicle that was not properly repaired
A driver striking an off-road vehicle

In Colorado, if another person or party caused your off-road recreational vehicle accident, that party may be financially responsible for your related injuries and losses. For example, all motor vehicle drivers in Colorado must carry car insurance to pay for the accidents that they cause. It is up to you or your attorney, however, to prove that the other party is liable before you can recover financial compensation for damages such as medical bills and property repairs.
